messages:
maya: quick heads up — ran `terraform plan` in staging and it wants to replace the kube config secret and recreate the service account in namespace payments after I ran `terraform import` earlier.

sam: did you import the secret or the SA? import usually misses cluster-populated annotations.

maya: imported `kubernetes_secret.redwood_payment_kubeconfig` with `terraform import kubernetes_secret.redwood_payment_kubeconfig default/redwood-payment-kubeconfig` then re-ran `plan` and saw this snippet:

maya: ```
# kubernetes_service_account.payment_sa will be replaced
-/+ resource "kubernetes_service_account" "payment_sa" {
  ~ metadata {
      - annotations = {
          "redwood/cache-prefix" = "staging:v1"
        } -> null
    }
}
```

jordan: paste the state show for that SA

maya: `terraform state show kubernetes_service_account.payment_sa` shows no annotations in state, but `kubectl get sa payment-sa -n payments -o yaml` shows `redwood/cache-prefix: staging:v1`.

ops-sre: that's the classic import mismatch — cluster added the annotation (maybe by init webhook) after creation so import didn't capture it. Two options: add the annotation to tf resource, or patch state.

sam: +1 to updating TF to include the annotation (sa resource metadata.annotations = { "redwood/cache-prefix" = "staging:v1" }). That keeps code as source of truth. State edit is faster but risky.

maya: I'll add the annotation in the resource and open a small PR. Will also include a note about the admission webhook behavior.

jordan: please also add a one-line migration note in infra/README so future imports don't surprise folks.

deploy-bot: Note: there is 1 pending plan in staging for PR #4823 — watcher set by @maya :eyes:

maya: thanks — if someone can watch the apply for any state lock/regional provisioning hiccups I'd appreciate it. I'll ping here when I kick it.

ops-sre: i'll keep an eye on the lock queue during your apply. ping me if it stalls.
